chunks: From him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Muskhan, from al-Hasan al-Siqqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: A man divorced his wife with a divorce that does not make her permissible to him until she marries another husband, and then she married him for a temporary marriage (mut'ah). Is she permissible to the first husband? He said: No.

Because Allah, the Exalted, says: 'So if he divorces her, she is not permissible to him afterwards until she marries another husband. So if he divorces her,' and the temporary marriage does not include a divorce.

key_terms.لَا تَحِلُّ لَهُ: She is not permissible to him
key_terms.وَالْمُتْعَةُ لَيْسَ فِيهَا طَلاقٌ: And temporary marriage does not include a divorce

ai.seo_question: Does temporary marriage (mut'ah) count as a valid marriage for the purpose of making a woman permissible to her first husband after a triple divorce?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Quranic condition for *tahlil* (making the wife permissible again) requires a genuine divorce (*talaq*) from the second husband, which temporary marriage (*mut'ah*) lacks by definition. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the permanence of marriage and the specific legal mechanics of divorce, ensuring the third divorce is not merely a formality but a substantive legal act.
